assumptions: Every figure is an ESTIMATE from the cost model in this module's docstring over the WP2 checker census; nothing is measured.  Widths in the binary model are upper bounds from value-magnitude tracking (a sum's bound is the sum of bounds), so adder widths exceed the true ones by 1-3 bits in places (the signed sum is tracked at 33-34 bits, true 30).

Small primes: F1 direct lt_pow as bound - 1 - x in [0, 2^B) is sound iff p >= 2^(B+1) - 1 given x in [0, 2^B); true for Mersenne31 at B = 30 exactly, false for BabyBear, which pays the signed-sum tightening (BABYBEAR_EXTRA).  Not verified with z3 in this lane; the checker's search.modular_queries is the place to do it.
Small primes: F3 (split normalisation) and F4 (word limbs) are hand-derived deltas (F3_SPLIT_PER_GROUP, F4_LIMBS_PER_UNIT), not re-derived by executing rewritten gadgets; the gadgets were not edited.

Small primes: accounting's census_estimate_* is reused with the field's per-unit figures; bytes are rescaled to 4-byte elements, field_ops stay in base-field multiplication equivalents (EXT_MULT_COST: degree 4 -> 9, 5 -> 13, 6 -> 17) and a Goldilocks-equivalent column assumes one 31-bit multiplication costs half a Goldilocks one (ESTIMATE); the layered shape and the internal-wire count of Candidate A are Goldilocks' (the small-field checker has 31 fewer products).

Binary tower: committed GF(2) elements are bits; bytes at Reed-Solomon rate 1/4 (Binius default), packed 128 bits per symbol; barrel shifts commit every mux stage; products of a bit and a value are w ANDs and stay virtual; 19 small-by-wide products the tracker cannot recognise as bits (the XOR-formed product sign) are costed as bit-schoolbook (an overcount of about 2,000 ANDs per unit).

Binary tower soundness: Lasso multiset check at (N + |T|)/2^128 per table plus a degree-2 zerocheck; the tower's top field in the crates is GF(2^128), so 2^-128 needs GF(2^256) (defined by the tower, not implemented) or repetition.

Latency and communication for the binary tower are modelled as a grand-product GKR chain of the LogUp-GKR shape plus a zerocheck; Ligero-style column openings at the same t as the Goldilocks operating point.

what_would_kill_each_option.goldilocks: nothing found here; the cubic extension reaches 2^-128 at every B, and it has the fewest field operations.
what_would_kill_each_option.m31 / babybear: 2^-128 at B = 4096 needs the degree-6 extension (or degree 5 with two lookup repetitions for Candidate A only: Candidate B's powers-combination term (n_lin - 1)/|F| floors at 2^-126.6 in 2^155); neither Plonky3 nor stwo ships a degree-5/6 M31 extension; the F1/F3/F4 repairs are unverified by z3; field_ops in Goldilocks equivalents are 1.4-2.7x the baseline at 2^-128 -- the halved bytes do not pay.
what_would_kill_each_option.binary tower: the checker is integer arithmetic: 712 adders per unit put 11,534 carry bits (50% of all committed bits) and 34,602 of 43,592 ANDs on the table, so committed bits (23,243/unit) exceed Goldilocks A's 321 x 64 = 20,544; logUp is unavailable (char 2); 2^-128 unreachable at GF(2^128); the original crate is archived and Binius64's 64-bit-word constraint system is a different arithmetisation than the one costed here.
